collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — BELIEF, IDENTITY AND PERSONAL EXPRESSION (BLF-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Religious, spiritual, atheist, agnostic, questioning and simply uninterested villagers living side by side; who people are, whom they love and how they present themselves. Privacy is respected, nobody has to explain or justify anything, and differences don't have to be the subject. Gods and spirits stay unconfirmed either way.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks two adults who fish)

collection.description: A villager thanks the sea for every fish, and their fishing partner finds it slightly maddening: tease them, or say nothing.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: Every time (subject) catches a fish, (subject.he/she) says a quiet thank you to the sea before (subject.he/she) puts it in the basket. Every single fish. (friend), who fishes beside (subject.him/her) and doesn't believe in thanking anything, has started to find it endearing and slightly maddening, especially on good days, when it slows everything down.

o1__fx.name: Outcome A
o1__fx.text: "Fourteen thank-yous already," says (friend). "The sea must be very polite by now." (subject) laughs. "Someone has to be." (friend) shakes (friend.his/her) head, grinning, and keeps fishing. By the end of the day (friend.he/she) catches (friend.him/her)self murmuring "thanks" to the water, very quietly. (friend.He/she) blames (subject) for it entirely.

o2__fx.name: Outcome B
o2__fx.text: (friend) says nothing and just waits each time. It's peaceful, actually. They fish side by side for hours, (subject) thanking every fish and (friend) watching the water. At the end of the day, they've caught the same number. (friend) still doesn't believe in thanking the sea. (friend.He/she) finds (friend.he/she) doesn't mind the waiting any more.
